title: Persistent Volatility History for Adaptive Warmup — Cycle 24
problem: Cycle 23's WarmupVolatilityTracker adapted predictive warmup TTL and scheduler interval from real chat send outcomes, but its rolling success/failure windows were in-memory only, so every app restart erased the learned signal.
root_cause: WarmupVolatilityTracker stored per-candidate Window arrays in actor memory with no persistence layer, ModelConfigurationStore did not expose volatility state, and ModelsTabView only showed in-memory adaptive controls.
fix: Added VolatilityHistoryStore actor that serializes WarmupVolatilityRecord structs to an encrypted JSON file using TriOSEncryption(keyName: warmup-volatility). Added stable stableKey serialization for CrossProviderModelCandidate. Wired the store into WarmupVolatilityTracker with async loadHistory/persist/reset and deterministic record() persistence. Updated ModelConfigurationStore to load history on init and expose volatility state helpers. Updated ModelsTabView with a learned-candidate indicator and reset button. Added VolatilityHistoryStoreTests and extended WarmupVolatilityTrackerTests.
next_options: Stale-while-revalidate send path — serve a slightly stale cached winner immediately while refreshing asynchronously
Per-conversation provider/model pinning — constrain adaptive warmup and failover within user-pinned boundaries per thread
Failure-kind-aware volatility — adjust TTL/interval per failure kind (auth, rate-limit, network, context-length)
learnings: Persisting small structured actor state as a single encrypted JSON blob keeps the change focused and avoids a SQLCipher schema migration when the data is not relational.
Adding a version + window-size field to the persisted record lets the tracker safely discard outdated or corrupt snapshots without blocking app startup.
Making record(_:for:) async and awaiting persist() directly removes fire-and-forget test races and guarantees the on-disk state matches the in-memory window after each send.
Stable ASCII candidate keys (provider|baseURL|model) are sufficient for volatility history because the tuple uniquely identifies the endpoint and is easy to validate on load.
